title: Payer Program Rules Read by the Equipment and Supply Lines — Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility
content:
**Digest.** Each Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility payer class carries the program rules that the equipment and supply lines read from the patient's primary coverage record. The class figures named below are those of the payer-class schedules.

## 1. Regime and allowed amounts

1.1 The class's payer family decides which notice, appeal and cost-share regime applies.

1.2 Contracted allowed amounts are the class's allowed-amount percentage of the fee schedule printed in each equipment or supply charter.

## 2. Rental caps

2.1 Capped-rental items transfer title after the class's capped-rental months, counted as paid months in one continuous rental period.

2.2 Oxygen equipment payments stop after the class's oxygen payment cap in paid months, and the supplier keeps furnishing oxygen equipment until the class's oxygen useful lifetime in months has passed from the first paid month.

## 3. Prior authorization and referral

3.1 Prior authorization is required before delivery of power mobility devices, before PAP setup, before oxygen setup, before hospital beds and powered surfaces, and before the first urological shipment — each where the class's grid marks that line as requiring it.

3.2 The payer decides a standard request within the class's standard decision period in calendar days and an expedited one within its expedited decision period in hours; an affirmed authorization is usable for the class's validity period in calendar days from its decision date.

3.3 Where the class requires a referral for DME, a primary-care referral must be on file before DME is billed.

## 4. Non-covered items and upgrades

4.1 An item expected to be denied, or an upgrade where the class permits upgrade billing, may be charged to the patient only after the patient signed the class's non-covered notice instrument before delivery.

4.2 Under "not permitted" the patient is never charged, and under "follows the primary" the primary's instrument governs.

## 5. Filing and appeals

5.1 A claim must reach the payer within the class's filing period in calendar days of the date of service.

5.2 A first-level appeal must be filed within the class's appeal window in calendar days of the denial and is decided within the class's appeal decision period.

## 6. Denials caused by the supplier

6.1 A line denied because Summit Ridge missed a prior authorization, a referral, the filing limit or a required notice is never charged to the patient; any charge posted for it is removed with the reason "missing-notice write-off".

## Points of judgement

| Fact | Consequence under this digest |
|---|---|
| Upgrade elected under a class that does not permit upgrade billing | clause 4.1 gives no basis to charge the upgrade to the patient |
| Item expected to be denied; class instrument "not permitted" | the patient is never charged |
| Secondary record with instrument "follows the primary" | the primary's instrument governs |
| Line denied because the claim missed the class's filing period | never charged to the patient; any posted charge removed as missing-notice write-off |
| Commercial HMO patient, authorization affirmed on day D (hypothetical) | usable for delivery for 60 calendar days from day D |
